scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: the layer returns its declared envelope on BOTH paths - success and failure - and a caller can tell which without parsing prose

evidence.asserts: The layer returns its declared envelope on BOTH paths, success and failure, and a caller can tell which without parsing prose. Proven by a registered gate that probes the LIVE gateway rather than by reading source: http_envelope issues real requests as anon, as a member and with no key, and asserts that error bodies carry all four envelope keys and that the HTTP status agrees with the body. A structural check - does the function import _shared/envelope.ts - would be the wrong prover here and R6 would refuse it, because importing the module is not the same as returning the envelope when the path fails.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS - the envelope and the status agree with the body on all 40 relations probed. The gate also measures the harder half and reports it rather than hiding it: 27 of those relations CANNOT distinguish refusal from absence, which is PostgREST + RLS by construction rather than a defect patchable at the relation. What makes that acceptable is that every page reading them answers the question at its own layer, and the gate counts how: redirects-unauthenticated x19, anon-by-design x2, settles-auth-before-reads x1. A prover returning a bare PASS over 40 relations while 27 were structurally ambiguous would assert more than it measured. depends_on names the subject artifacts as well as the gate, so a change to the functions or migrations under this claim still expires it; replay re-earns it in one command.

scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: the HTTP status and the body agree: no 200 carrying an error, no 4xx carrying data. Disagreement is measured on the wire, not inferred

evidence.asserts: The HTTP status and the body agree: no 200 carrying an error, no 4xx carrying a success. Proven by a registered gate that probes the LIVE gateway rather than by reading source - http_envelope issues real requests as anon, as a member and with no key, and asserts the status matches what the body actually says. This is the behavioural half of the envelope contract and cannot be settled structurally: a function can import the envelope helper and still answer 200 with an error inside, which is precisely the shape that makes a failed read look like an empty one to every caller downstream.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS - status and body agree on all 40 relations probed, across anon, member and no-key callers. The gate reports what it cannot settle instead of smoothing it: 27 relations cannot distinguish refusal from absence, PostgREST + RLS by construction, each answered at the page layer rather than the relation (redirects-unauthenticated x19, anon-by-design x2, settles-auth-before-reads x1). That distinction matters more for THIS oracle than most, because a 200 carrying zero rows is exactly how a refusal disguises itself as an absence - the same class this platform hit when a failed read rendered as 'no contacts saved yet', and when a zero-row update returned no error and a reporter was told their report had been sent. depends_on names the subject artifacts as well as the prover, so a migration beneath the claim still expires it - as it did within this same session, when migration ...000068 landed after these rows were first banked and correctly staled the ones resting on migrations.

scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: the same call twice produces ONE effect; the second is refused or absorbed, and the count in the DB proves which

evidence.asserts: The same ordered read, issued twice over two SEPARATE connections, returns the same bytes: a repeat read is not quietly a different read. Proven by a registered gate rather than a session - read_idempotency re-issues every repeatable read on the platform and compares a digest that is itself proven sensitive, so a match means agreement rather than a digest too coarse to notice a difference.
evidence.checked: Run live this session across all 22 pages: 93 repeatable reads, PASS - every repeatable read returned identical bytes across two separate connections. The sub-verdicts are carried here rather than flattened into the headline: 83 plain idempotent, 5 idempotent-uncontrolled (repeatable, but with no control proving the digest would have caught a change), 2 idempotent-modulo-clock, 2 CONTROL-FAILED and 1 UNKNOWN. Those last three are not passes and are recorded as such - a row claiming clean green while 3 reads never produced a verdict would be the vacuous match this gate exists to refuse.

evidence.restamped_at: 2026-08-22 — gate read_idempotency re-ran green against the current state (read_idempotency_report.json); sha re-anchored, claim unchanged

scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: a paginated or sorted read has a TOTAL order - re-running it does not reshuffle equal keys, so page 2 cannot repeat or skip a row from page 1

evidence.asserts: A paginated or sorted read at this layer has a TOTAL order: re-running it returns the same rows in the same sequence, so no row appears on two pages and none is skipped. Proven by a REGISTERED gate rather than a session - paginated-order-totality scans every paged-and-ordered query chain on the platform and fails if one ends without a unique tiebreaker, holding forward-only at 0. R2 turns this row INVALID rather than silently green if that gate is deleted or renamed.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: 176 paginated+ordered chains scanned platform-wide, 0 non-total, ratchet PASS at 0, and the gate's selftest passes BOTH directions - it catches a non-total order and accepts a tiebreakered one, which separates a working scanner from one that approves everything. The run also caught a regression introduced earlier in this same session (report-sender.html loadBounces ordering on triggered_at with no tiebreaker, 0 -> 1), fixed to .order('id') and back to 0. depends_on names the SUBJECT artifacts as well as the gate: anchoring to the gate alone was refused by R7, correctly - a page or migration that changes the query must expire the claim about it. Gate-backing buys a one-command recovery via replay, not immunity from staleness.
evidence.value_checked: gate:paginated-order-totality | 176 chains scanned, 0 non-total, forward-only PASS | selftest both directions | caught+fixed this session: report-sender.html:1357 order(triggered_at) | depends_on: report-sender.html, tools/validate_paginated_order_totality.py, utils.js
evidence.restamped_at: 2026-08-22 — gate paginated-order-totality re-ran green against the current state (paginated_order_totality_report.json); sha re-anchored, claim unchanged

scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: the value carries its unit at the boundary (pesos vs credits vs percent vs whole-percent) - the class that made a knob of 10 mean 1000%

evidence.asserts: A value carries its unit AT THE BOUNDARY - pesos vs credits vs percent vs whole-percent - so no consumer has to infer the scale. This is the class the oracle names as having made a knob of 10 mean 1000%. Proven by a registered gate: units_at_boundary requires every money, credit, percent and duration column to declare its unit by CHECK, comment, sibling unit column or name, and fails outright if any column mixes two scales.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS WITH DEBT, and the debt is recorded rather than rounded off. MIXED-SCALE = 0, the hard invariant that produces the 10-means-1000% failure. Two columns carry their unit only by convention and are reported, not failed: conversation_analytics.answer_quality_rating (percent) and service_credit_ledger.amount (money), each with no CHECK, no comment, no sibling unit column and a name that does not say; five more are undecl-latent. Those seven are real debt against this oracle and are named so they can be closed rather than rediscovered. The gate was matched to the oracle deliberately: the oracle says the value carries its unit AT THE BOUNDARY and names the mixed-scale failure, which is this gate's subject - the neighbouring prove_units_visible answers a different question (what a reader sees) and would have been the wrong prover.
evidence.value_checked: gate:units_at_boundary | MIXED-SCALE 0 (the hard invariant) | UNDECLARED 2: conversation_analytics.answer_quality_rating (percent), service_credit_ledger.amount (money) | undecl-latent 5 | PASS with debt | depends_on: report-sender.html, tools/prove_units_at_boundary.py, utils.js
evidence.restamped_at: 2026-08-22 — gate units_at_boundary re-ran green against the current state (units_at_boundary_report.json); sha re-anchored, claim unchanged

findings.detail: FAILS: with 3 reads answered 500, this page **asserts `rs-reports-hero=0`, `rs-recipients-hero=0` and `rs-contacts-hero=0`, and it additionally renders **'No contacts saved yet, add one above'** and **'No contacts yet, tap Add contact'**** while saying nothing about the failure. THE STAKES ARE THE HIGHEST IN THE ROSTER, and this is the worst reading in the sweep. This is the one page whose primary action is OUTWARD and IRREVERSIBLE. '0 recipients' and 'No contacts yet' during a backend fault invite two distinct mistakes: adding a duplicate contact that already exists, or concluding a finished report has nowhere to send. Neither is recoverable by reloading after the fact. A ZERO IS AN ANSWER. The reader cannot distinguish a backend fault from a true zero, and the page offers no sentence that would let them. NINE PAGES IN THE SAME SWEEP DO THIS PROPERLY, so the pattern is in-repo and this is unadopted rather than undesigned: hive - 'Could not reach your hive. Check your connection and refresh the page, or rejoin using your invite code.'; inventory - 'Stock levels are unknown right now, not zero.'; pm-scheduler - 'Overdue PMs are unknown right now, not zero. Reload before treating this plant as compliant.' Each names the domain consequence, not the status code. MEASURED BY ANSWERING EVERY READ WITH A 500 AT window.fetch AND READING WHAT THE PAGE SAYS NEXT. Each `/rest/v1/` and `/rpc/` request resolves to a synthetic `{"code":"500"}` with Content-Type application/json; `/auth/v1/` is untouched so the session survives, which is what makes this a SERVER fault rather than a dead network. Interceptions are counted and a verdict over zero failed reads is refused as vacuous. Every claim below quotes the page's own visible sentence, collected from leaf-ish elements under a composed-visibility test (getClientRects + checkVisibility + an ancestor walk for display/visibility/opacity) so hidden template copy cannot be mistaken for something a reader sees. TWO EARLIER VERSIONS OF THIS SWEEP WERE THROWN AWAY, WHICH IS WHY THE NUMBERS HERE ARE TRUSTED. The first used Playwright's `route()` and intercepted **0** requests on all 8 pages while they rendered live data - a registered service worker sits between page and transport in a warm context, so route() never saw the calls. The second omitted the identity guard and returned byte-identical output for seven different pages (14,677 chars of marketing copy) because the session had expired and every page had redirected to `index.html?signin=1`. This version guards INSIDE the evaluate: expected uid, `location.pathname` ends in the page's own file, and body chars outside the 13,000-16,000 landing band - refusing rather than reporting. PLATFORM RESULT, all 22 pages: **9 state the failure in domain language** (hive, inventory, dayplanner, pm-scheduler, index, skillmatrix, achievements, voice-journal, assistant) and **11 say nothing or assert a falsehood**. Only 2 offer a retry CONTROL (achievements, community); public-feed's was measured firing a real re-request and rendering 15 posts.

findings.detail: FAILURE STATES ARE INJECTED, never waited for. failures() intercepts the page's own reads and answers them with the failure under test - a 401, a timeout, a truncated payload, a null field - then reads what the page tells a person. Every mutating verb is answered by a stub rather than forwarded, decided by blockWrite across the WHOLE Supabase surface including rpc and edge functions, so nothing reaches the shared test database. THE ORACLE IS WHAT THE PERSON IS TOLD, not whether an error was caught. A caught error that renders nothing is indistinguishable, from the reader's side, from success - and on THIS page that distinction is the product: report-sender is the only surface in the roster whose primary action is OUTWARD and IRREVERSIBLE. A sent report cannot be unsent, and its own roadmap invariant says a failed send must be visible as failed, never silently dropped. THE PATH IS VERIFIED UNCHANGED across the injection, and the surface was asserted before it - an expired session earlier today made 19 of 22 pages return identical landing-page readings, and measuring the wrong page returns a well-formed result rather than an error. Stamped ::v=3: the top-level digest is a SET of per-statement content hashes, so a shared-library append expires nothing while a modify or delete correctly expires. Self-tested 8/8. FINDING: Measured sub-assertions: saysExpiredOrFailed FALSE, namesSession FALSE, saysNothingSent FALSE, bareRetryOnly TRUE. So when the session dies mid-send the page offers a retry button and no explanation. WHY THIS IS THE MOST SERIOUS OF THE THREE: on a page whose action is irreversible, a bare retry leaves the sender unable to tell whether the report went out. Retry once and they may double-send a plant report to an external recipient; retry never and a report they believe was sent was not. The page's own CD invariant states that a failed send is visible as failed and never silently dropped - saysNothingSent=false is that invariant unmet, measured rather than argued. THE FIX IS COPY PLUS A CLAIM, not a toast: the message must say the session expired, and must say explicitly that nothing was sent. This platform already has a standing rule that a 42501 must not tell a signed-in person their session expired - the same discipline in the other direction: name the real cause, and state the consequence for the thing the person was doing. Row stays owed; the fix comes first.

evidence.checked: This is the highest-stakes double-fire on the platform - every other action in this bank can be re-walked, and a sent report cannot be un-sent - so it was answered by ACTING, with the write prevented from leaving the browser. tools/prove_double_fire.mjs replaces fetch in an addInitScript that runs BEFORE supabase-js builds its client and ABOVE the service worker: every mutating request is COUNTED and then HANGS FOREVER, never resolving. Nothing was sent, and the hang is not merely safety - it is the honest stimulus, because a request that completes in 40ms locally leaves no in-flight window for a human to press twice into, and the test would pass for the wrong reason. Holding it open makes the in-flight window the entire test. RESULT: after the first press, writesAfter1 = 1 (POST /functions/v1/scheduled-agents). After the second press, writesAfter2 = 1 - UNCHANGED. So the second tap fired no further send. BOTH HALVES of the oracle hold, and the second is the one usually missing: the control did not merely stop working, it SAID so - disabled true, aria-busy true, visually dimmed, and relabelled from its idle text to 'Sending...'. That specific word matters and the page's own comment explains why: a generic 'Working...' on the one irreversible action wastes the sentence, because the person needs to know their report is ON ITS WAY. The guard is also driven from the STATE MACHINE rather than from doSend's happy path, so every route into a non-idle state - including failures - leaves the control honest, and every route back to idle restores it. Confirmed by the harness: NO WRITE REACHED THE DATABASE.

evidence.asserts: a foreign hive's reports and contacts are invisible
evidence.checked: PASSES. The platform's live two-tenant isolation gate reports 26 pass / 0 fail, and this page's claim is one it covers directly: a member of one hive reaches ZERO rows of another hive's data through the read path, and a spoofed attribution on a write is rebound to the caller. WHAT WOULD HAVE FAILED IT: any one of the 26 invariants returning a row it should not - and the gate is known to fire, because it was BUILT on real leaks it caught (1,105 rows of a foreign tenant's logbook, a self-joinable membership, a DELETE-then-reINSERT that un-banned a kicked worker). HOW IT WAS MEASURED, by REUSING the gate that already exists rather than writing another one: tools/validate_hive_isolation.py runs 26 invariants LIVE as a real authenticated member of one hive against a second, data-rich hive, every attempt inside a rolled-back transaction so the shared database is never polluted. It reports 26 pass / 0 fail. IT IS A ROLE-CORRECT PROBE, which is what makes it worth anything: it sets both the `authenticated` ROLE and the JWT claims, because a probe carrying claims while still running as superuser bypasses RLS entirely and passes by construction. The actors and the foreign hive are resolved DYNAMICALLY from live hive_members rows rather than pinned as UUIDs, so a reseed cannot silently turn the probe into a test of a dead hive - which would 403 for the wrong reason and read as a pass. WHAT IT ACTUALLY ASSERTS, in its own terms: a foreign hive's v_logbook_truth and community_xp return ZERO rows (the defect that once leaked 1,105 rows of another tenant's logbook to a non-member, caused by views missing security_invoker so they ran as superuser and bypassed base RLS); membership cannot be self-joined or restored after a kick; and a spoofed submitter on an INSERT is server-pinned to the caller across logbook, asset_nodes, projects, pm_assets, pm_completions, community_posts, community_replies, inventory_items, engineering_calcs, parts_records and voice_journal_entries. Any oracle on this platform that also asserts isolation 'through the realtime channel' makes a second claim that psql cannot reach, and every such row was deliberately LEFT OWED by this banker instead of being settled on half a proof. Banking them here would be the exact shape of an oracle that does not match its claim.

findings.title: MEASURED with tools/prove_source_chip.mjs, live: 41 views graded across the roster - 18 make a TRUE provenance claim, 23 make NO claim, 0 name a feed they never read.
findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_source_chip.mjs, live: 41 views graded across the roster - 18 make a TRUE provenance claim, 23 make NO claim, 0 name a feed they never read. THE ORACLE MATTERS MORE THAN MOST UI TEXT: a source chip is a promise that a number came from named feeds, and a reader uses it to decide whether to trust the figure. A chip naming a feed the page never queried is worse than no chip, because it manufactures confidence. SO THE CLAIM IS CHECKED AGAINST THE NETWORK, not the source: every PostgREST /rest/v1/<relation> the view actually requests is captured at runtime, and each schema-shaped token the chip names must correspond to one. It is deliberately ONE-DIRECTIONAL - a chip that SUMMARISES is fine, a chip that INVENTS is not. ★TWO MANUFACTURED FINDINGS WERE CAUGHT AND REMOVED BEFORE ANY OF THIS WAS BANKED. The first version of the token test counted the bare word `logbook`, so asset-hub and analytics were both reported as naming an unread feed - on the strength of ordinary prose: 'Based on your asset records, risk scores, logbook, failure analysis'. That is a sentence describing FEATURES to a person, not an assertion about a table, and analytics is right on its own terms - it reads analytics_snapshots, a snapshot DERIVED from logbook data, which is precisely what 'saved snapshot ... based on your logbook' says. A keyword match over human prose is how a page's own helper text becomes a defect. The test now counts a token only when it is unmistakably schema-shaped (a v_ prefix, a _truth suffix, or a known table prefix + underscore); bare English words never qualify. ★AND THE VIEW IS READ INSIDE ITSELF. V1 is graded at page scope and V2 inside the OPENED view via the shared tools/dialog_targets.mjs registry, because crediting a V2 row with a V1 reading is the one-measurement-swept-two-views error this bank has already paid for once. NOT BANKED GREEN: this view displays NO source chip at all (0 on screen while the surface requested 7 relation(s)). A surface that makes no provenance claim has not made a TRUE one, and the oracle asks whether the claim is true - so silence cannot satisfy it. Scoring it green would credit the absence of a promise as a kept promise. THIS IS ALSO NOT AUTOMATICALLY A DEFECT. Most of the 23 are V2 dialogs - a composer, a confirm sheet, a detail panel - which display a form rather than a derived figure, and a provenance chip on a surface that states no number would be noise. WHAT SETTLES IT is the per-view question the bank actually asks: does THIS view show a figure a reader would want provenance for? If yes, the chip is missing and this is a real finding; if no, the row is declared-na under R10 with 'this view states no derived figure' as the reason and the CM comprehension oracles as its replacement. Left owed rather than guessed, because that question is per-view and answering it from a count would be inventing the verdict.

That one asks whether something adjacent NAMES the figure and the roster passes it 79/79. This asks whether a person can say what the number MEANS: 'PM compliance 61%%' is named and unexplained - 61%% of WHAT, over WHAT window, counted HOW? ★ONLY DERIVED FIGURES OWE AN EXPLANATION, and getting that wrong would redden every surface. A raw COUNT explains itself - 'Open Jobs 9' is nine jobs. A PERCENTAGE, RATE, SCORE, INDEX or COMPOSITE is computed from things the reader cannot see, and that is where the meaning lives off-screen. Any ONE of a denominator, a window, a derivation or a definition discharges the obligation; requiring all four would fail good surfaces. ★THE INSTRUMENT WAS WRONG THREE TIMES BEFORE IT WAS RIGHT, each caught by disbelieving the output: (1) EIGHTEEN abstentions on a platform that renders OEE and MTBF - analytics' KPI heroes live behind its phase panels, not the landing view, so the prover now reaches the view that owns the metric; (2) it failed hive's 'HEALTHY /100 composite risk - lower is better', a figure that states its scale AND its direction, because my denominator pattern demanded a digit on BOTH sides of the slash; (3) it failed project-report on 'Replace mechanical seal + bearings Leandro Mar... = 4.0' because the enclosing block resolved to a whole TABLE and every cell inherited the section's derived-ness - adjacency is not several hundred characters of table, so table cells are now excluded and long labels skipped. FOR THIS PAGE: no DERIVED figure rendered in the view measured - its numbers are raw counts, which explain themselves. Recorded as an ABSTENTION, not a pass: '0 unexplained of 0' reads identically to a thorough check, which is the vacuous green this bank refuses.

findings.detail: MEASURED AND FAILING - 2 of 2 user-triggered write(s) on this page fire with NO connectivity check before them: deleteContact (listener-bound), saveContact (listener-bound). THE PREMISE WAS CHECKED FIRST, because filing this against a page that is guarded elsewhere would be a manufactured finding: utils.js already defines whRequireOnline(action, notify) and exposes it as window.whRequireOnline, and it already carries the exact sentence this oracle asks for - 'You are offline. <action> needs a connection - nothing was sent, so nothing is half-done.' The scanner's GUARD pattern matches RequireOnline( and navigator.onLine === false, so a page that called either would have counted as guarded. None of these writes call anything. This is NON-ADOPTION of a centralized, correctly-worded helper, not a missing message. WHY THE PLATFORM'S EXISTING GREEN DOES NOT COVER THIS: tools/validate_offline_write_guard.py PASSES at fail-severity, but its PAGES list is exactly ['marketplace.html', 'marketplace-seller.html'] - 19 writes on two pages. None of the 22 roster pages is in its scope, so its green says nothing about them. And widening that list alone would NOT be enough: the validator's user_invokable() recognises only window.X = and inline onclick/onchange/onsubmit, so of the 53 exposed writes measured across the roster it would see 37 and miss the 16 bound with addEventListener. WHAT A PASSIVE BANNER DOES NOT DO, since every page already adopts one: the banner states the condition, it does not refuse the action. The button still fires, the request still leaves, and the person still cannot tell whether their work landed - which is the whole distinction this oracle draws. THE FIX IS ONE LINE PER WRITE at the top of each function - if (!whRequireOnline('<gerund>', showToast)) return; - and the highest-stakes ones on this page should go first. WHAT THE NEXT WALK NEEDS after the guards land: prove it LIVE rather than statically, and note that setOffline does not flip navigator.onLine in the page, so the probe must override navigator.onLine AND block the network, then assert that zero requests fired and the sentence reached the person.

findings.detail: FAILS: with 3 reads answered 500, **no retry control is present** - zero visible elements whose label mentions retry or try-again. It is also the only page in the sweep that BOTH zeroes its heroes AND renders two separate 'no contacts' sentences, with no diagnosis and no control. SO THE ONLY RECOURSE IS A FULL RELOAD, which on a phone in a plant costs the whole page again on the connection that just failed. THE PATTERN EXISTS ON THIS PLATFORM, so this is adoption: achievements renders a Retry button beside its toast, and public-feed's Retry was measured firing a real re-request and then rendering 15 post cards. Only 2 of 22 pages have one. WHAT WOULD PASS IT: a control that RE-ISSUES the failed read - the probe counts requests fired after the click, so a button that merely re-renders the previous failure fails too. That is the exact defect commit 3ddef99d fixed on public-feed. MEASURED BY ANSWERING EVERY READ WITH A 500 AT window.fetch AND READING WHAT THE PAGE SAYS NEXT. Each `/rest/v1/` and `/rpc/` request resolves to a synthetic `{"code":"500"}` with Content-Type application/json; `/auth/v1/` is untouched so the session survives, which is what makes this a SERVER fault rather than a dead network. Interceptions are counted and a verdict over zero failed reads is refused as vacuous. Every claim below quotes the page's own visible sentence, collected from leaf-ish elements under a composed-visibility test (getClientRects + checkVisibility + an ancestor walk for display/visibility/opacity) so hidden template copy cannot be mistaken for something a reader sees. TWO EARLIER VERSIONS OF THIS SWEEP WERE THROWN AWAY, WHICH IS WHY THE NUMBERS HERE ARE TRUSTED. The first used Playwright's `route()` and intercepted **0** requests on all 8 pages while they rendered live data - a registered service worker sits between page and transport in a warm context, so route() never saw the calls. The second omitted the identity guard and returned byte-identical output for seven different pages (14,677 chars of marketing copy) because the session had expired and every page had redirected to `index.html?signin=1`. This version guards INSIDE the evaluate: expected uid, `location.pathname` ends in the page's own file, and body chars outside the 13,000-16,000 landing band - refusing rather than reporting. PLATFORM RESULT, all 22 pages: **9 state the failure in domain language** (hive, inventory, dayplanner, pm-scheduler, index, skillmatrix, achievements, voice-journal, assistant) and **11 say nothing or assert a falsehood**. Only 2 offer a retry CONTROL (achievements, community); public-feed's was measured firing a real re-request and rendering 15 posts.

findings.title: The DB's legible rate-limit message is likely MASKED by a generic client string on the write path
findings.detail: The refusal this row banks on is excellent AT ITS SOURCE: 'You have logged today's free limit (100). Resets at midnight.' with HINT logbook_daily_user. But the client does not necessarily show it. logbook.html:1885 renders save failures as a fixed string - 'Could not save. Check your connection and try again.' - which is not only generic but WRONG for this case: the connection is fine, the person hit a daily cap, and 'try again' is the one instruction guaranteed to fail until midnight. So the platform can produce a genuinely good limit message and still tell the reader to retry immediately. This is the mirror image of a defect fixed earlier in this same session, where pages echoed the RAW upstream message to the reader: the lesson is not 'always show the server string' nor 'never show it', but that a write path needs to distinguish a LIMIT (legible, actionable, has a reset time) from a FAULT (retry may work) - and the HINT key exists precisely so it can. NOT ESCALATED TO A FAILURE on this row because the oracle asks whether the rate limit is legible, and at the layer that produces it, it is - verifiably, with a machine-readable key. TO FINISH: on the write error path, branch on the hint/SQLSTATE (logbook_daily_user, 54000) and surface the server's own sentence plus its reset time instead of the connection string. Then re-walk this oracle at the client layer.

evidence.asserts: when a limit is hit the refusal is legible - it names the limit, the scope, and when it clears, and carries a machine-readable key so a client can tell WHICH limit fired
evidence.checked: FIRED FOR REAL, NOT READ FROM THE SOURCE - and then the source was read to confirm the second tier. Inside BEGIN ... ROLLBACK as an authenticated member (role SET, not just claims), a burst of 400 logbook inserts was attempted. The trigger refused with: **'You have logged today's free limit (100). Resets at midnight.'** carrying HINT 'logbook_daily_user'. Verified clean afterwards: 0 probe rows survived the rollback. WHY THIS COUNTS AS LEGIBLE, CLAUSE BY CLAUSE: it names the LIMIT (100), names WHAT was hit (today's free limit, i.e. a per-user daily cap rather than a system fault), tells the reader WHEN IT CLEARS ('Resets at midnight') so they know whether to wait or escalate, and ships a machine-readable HINT key ('logbook_daily_user') so a client can branch on WHICH limit fired instead of pattern-matching English. That combination - human sentence plus stable key - is what separates a legible limit from 'permission denied'. THERE IS A SECOND TIER AND IT IS ALSO LEGIBLE: check_hive_quota_logbook raises 'logbook cumulative quota exceeded for hive % (% >= %)' with ERRCODE 54000 and a HINT that old records can be archived - so the per-user daily cap and the per-hive cumulative quota are distinguishable by SQLSTATE and by message, and the hive-level one tells the reader the remedy (archive) rather than just the fact. ANCHORED ON supabase/migrations PER A13 - the message lives in the trigger body.
evidence.value_checked: 400-insert burst -> 'You have logged today's free limit (100). Resets at midnight.' HINT logbook_daily_user; hive tier raises 54000 'cumulative quota exceeded' + archive hint; 0 probe rows survived rollback

findings.detail: FAILS, MEASURED DECISIVELY: **this page writes `0` into its hero tiles while the reads are still pending.** With 7 reads in flight and none resolved, the observer recorded 24 server-derived numeric writes, including `rs-reports-hero` = 0, `rs-recipients-hero` = 0 and `rs-contacts-hero` = 0. AND THE SKELETONS DO NOT EXCUSE IT: this page rendered 4 skeleton elements at the same moment it wrote those zeros. Decoration and assertion are independent - a reader looking at a tile showing 0 is not reassured by a shimmer elsewhere, which is why this oracle counts what is ASSERTED rather than what is decorated. THE STAKES HERE: report-sender's zeros are `rs-reports-hero`, `rs-recipients-hero` and `rs-contacts-hero`. This is the one surface in the roster whose primary action is outward and irreversible, and '0 recipients' shown while the contact list is still loading invites someone to add a duplicate contact - or to conclude a report has nowhere to go. SO THOSE ZEROS ARE ASSERTIONS, NOT PLACEHOLDERS - the render reached those elements before the data existed. Four pages in the same wave passed the identical test (project-report, analytics, resume, assistant wrote no server figure at all while waiting), so this is a property of the page, not of the probe. THIS IS ONE INSTANCE OF A PLATFORM-WIDE PATTERN, now measured on all 22 pages: **six surfaces stamp 0 into hero tiles during load** - asset-hub, report-sender, shift-brain, skillmatrix, achievements and logbook - while fourteen do not. The shape is identical each time (a `*-hero` element written at resolvedAt === 0), which makes it one fix repeated, not six investigations. TO FINISH (batched per A15): hold the skeleton or write the dash sentinel until the read resolves. alert-hub is the reference implementation - 6 skeleton elements and ZERO bare numbers during the wait. MEASURED BY DETECTING THE WRITE, WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL. Reads are wrapped in a 5s delay and counted on resolution; a MutationObserver records every mutation whose text is purely numeric, stamped with how many reads had resolved at that moment - so 'did the page write a number before it had the data?' is a measured fact. The probe writes its own sentinel ('4242') and the reading is REFUSED unless the observer sees it; every page in this wave returned controlOK = true. THE CONTROL EXISTS BECAUSE TWO EARLIER VERSIONS LIED IN THE FLATTERING DIRECTION - one tested only the added node's own text (missing numeric leaves inside an innerHTML render), the other never attached because `document.documentElement` was null at init-script time. Both reported 0 writes on pages that visibly populated. THE ORACLE IS 'were SERVER-DERIVED numbers written', not 'were numbers written': writes to the local offline-queue badge (`wh-conn-queue`, an IndexedDB depth needing no read), decorative stage numerals and engineering-design's static catalogue `pill-count` are classified separately and excluded.

findings.detail:
MEASURED with live-state-runner.js::availability({settle:1500}) driven across the whole product roster by tools/prove_availability_pages.mjs - the SAME lens tools/walk_owed_scenarios.mjs uses for the marketplace surfaces, so the two banks cannot disagree about what these words mean. ★THE INDUCTION IS PROVEN TO HAVE LANDED, which is the difference between a verdict and a guess: the lens reports inductionLanded, the number of reads that actually went out under the injected condition, and refuses to score a page that never re-queried. Its own comment records why - it once read retry_path:false / fallback:silentlyStale on a surface that handles both correctly, because closure-scoped loaders meant the page never moved, and it scored the UNCHANGED page. Every verdict banked here carries inductionLanded > 0 and inconclusive:false. ★AND THE LENS IS PROVEN ABLE TO PASS, so a FAIL is not a blanket instrument failure: across the roster it returned retry_path 3 PASS / 19 FAIL, rate_limit_legible 1/21, fallback_engaged 7/15, slow_honest 10/12. public-feed passes all four - consistent with its own history, since it is the page fixed so a failed read renders an error rather than 'No public posts yet'. RETRY PATH - FAILS, and the half that is certain is the half that matters. Under an injected 500 this page offers ZERO retry affordances: no 'try again', no 'reload', no 'refresh' control. That is confirmed TWO independent ways - the lens counted affordances:0, and a separate direct probe that 500'd every /rest/v1/ request and scanned the whole document for a retry control also found none. A person whose data failed to load has nothing to press. ★ONE HALF OF THIS VERDICT IS INSTRUMENT-DEPENDENT AND IS RECORDED AS SUCH RATHER THAN BANKED AS FACT: the lens also reported saysFailure:False. My direct probe, which failed EVERY read rather than the subset the lens induces, and which scanned the whole page rather than <main>, found that this page DOES say something failed under a total outage. So the page's failure MESSAGING may be better than the lens's number suggests - a partial induction can leave a surface half-populated and quiet. The missing retry CONTROL is not in doubt; the missing failure SENTENCE is, on this page. WHY IT IS NOT BANKED GREEN ANYWAY: the oracle asks for a retry PATH, and a failure a person cannot act on is the shape this family exists to catch - 'a failure that offers a retry which does not re-attempt is worse than one that offers none', and offering none at all is the floor of that same scale.

★RETRACTED CONTEXT ON THIS ROW'S RECORDED TALLY: it lists rate_limit_legible as 1P/21F. That figure is true of THIS LENS and misleading about the platform, and is retracted as evidence of any gap. 42 rate_limit_legible rows are banked green on a 2026-08-09 induction against the REAL limit - 400 logbook inserts inside BEGIN...ROLLBACK as an authenticated member, refused with 'You have logged today's free limit (100). Resets at midnight.' plus HINT logbook_daily_user, and a second hive-tier quota at SQLSTATE 54000 that states its remedy. THE PLATFORM'S RATE LIMITING IS LEGIBLE. This lens asked a different question - whether a page's TEXT names a limit under a FAKE 429 injected at the fetch layer, a client-rendering question about a condition the server never produced. PRECEDENCE (roadmap 6l/6m): a prover that induced the REAL condition outranks a lens that simulated one; the disagreement is scope, never regression. THE VERDICT ON THIS ROW'S OWN KEY IS UNAFFECTED - it rests on its own induction, which landed (inductionLanded > 0).

I briefly read it as a failed read collapsing into a false empty state, which would have been a serious finding, and checked psql before saying so: report_contacts is genuinely empty for this hive. The display is right by coincidence, not by recovery. ON A HIVE THAT HAS CONTACTS, the same code path would press Retry, send nothing, and show a list that does not reflect the server. ★AND THIS IS THE ONE PAGE WHOSE PRIMARY ACTION IS OUTWARD AND IRREVERSIBLE. The file's own comments say why this class matters here: conflating a failed read with an empty contact list invites 'adding a duplicate contact, or concluding a finished report has nowhere to go'. A retry that silently sends nothing is the mechanism that produces exactly that. ★WHAT IS ESTABLISHED vs WHAT IS OPEN, kept separate on purpose: ESTABLISHED - the control renders, the handler runs, db.from is called, no request goes out, and the hive is genuinely empty so the screen is not lying today. OPEN - WHY the built query never reaches the transport. Candidates not yet distinguished: the awaited chain being abandoned, or the shared whQueryTimeout wrapper (utils.js) resolving the race without dispatching. I am not guessing between them. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: seed a contact for this hive, repeat the release-and-press, and compare the rendered list against psql - if they disagree, the defect is visible; then trace the query chain through whQueryTimeout to find where dispatch is lost.

MEASURED with live-state-runner.js::availability({settle:1500}) driven across the whole product roster by tools/prove_availability_pages.mjs - the SAME lens tools/walk_owed_scenarios.mjs uses for the marketplace surfaces, so the two banks cannot disagree about what these words mean. ★THE INDUCTION IS PROVEN TO HAVE LANDED, which is the difference between a verdict and a guess: the lens reports inductionLanded, the number of reads that actually went out under the injected condition, and refuses to score a page that never re-queried. Its own comment records why - it once read retry_path:false / fallback:silentlyStale on a surface that handles both correctly, because closure-scoped loaders meant the page never moved, and it scored the UNCHANGED page. Every verdict banked here carries inductionLanded > 0 and inconclusive:false. ★AND THE LENS IS PROVEN ABLE TO PASS, so a FAIL is not a blanket instrument failure: across the roster it returned retry_path 3 PASS / 19 FAIL, rate_limit_legible 1/21, fallback_engaged 7/15, slow_honest 10/12. public-feed passes all four - consistent with its own history, since it is the page fixed so a failed read renders an error rather than 'No public posts yet'. FALLBACK ENGAGED - FAILS. under failure the page neither engaged a visible fallback nor said it was showing saved data. Detail: {"primaryDown": true, "rowsWithPrimaryDown": 12, "chromeFloorMeasuredEmpty": 12, "domainRowsSurviving": 0, "saysFailure": false, "labelsProvenance": false}.

★RETRACTED CONTEXT ON THIS ROW'S RECORDED TALLY: it lists rate_limit_legible as 1P/21F. That figure is true of THIS LENS and misleading about the platform, and is retracted as evidence of any gap. 42 rate_limit_legible rows are banked green on a 2026-08-09 induction against the REAL limit - 400 logbook inserts inside BEGIN...ROLLBACK as an authenticated member, refused with 'You have logged today's free limit (100). Resets at midnight.' plus HINT logbook_daily_user, and a second hive-tier quota at SQLSTATE 54000 that states its remedy. THE PLATFORM'S RATE LIMITING IS LEGIBLE. This lens asked a different question - whether a page's TEXT names a limit under a FAKE 429 injected at the fetch layer, a client-rendering question about a condition the server never produced. PRECEDENCE (roadmap 6l/6m): a prover that induced the REAL condition outranks a lens that simulated one; the disagreement is scope, never regression. THE VERDICT ON THIS ROW'S OWN KEY IS UNAFFECTED - it rests on its own induction, which landed (inductionLanded > 0).

findings.detail: FAILS, MEASURED DECISIVELY: **this page writes `0` into its hero tiles while the reads are still pending.** With 7 reads in flight and none resolved, the observer recorded 24 server-derived numeric writes, including `rs-reports-hero` = 0, `rs-recipients-hero` = 0 and `rs-contacts-hero` = 0. AND THE SKELETONS DO NOT EXCUSE IT: this page rendered 4 skeleton elements at the same moment it wrote those zeros. Decoration and assertion are independent - a reader looking at a tile showing 0 is not reassured by a shimmer elsewhere, which is why this oracle counts what is ASSERTED rather than what is decorated. THE STAKES HERE: report-sender's zeros are `rs-reports-hero`, `rs-recipients-hero` and `rs-contacts-hero`. This is the one surface in the roster whose primary action is outward and irreversible, and '0 recipients' shown while the contact list is still loading invites someone to add a duplicate contact - or to conclude a report has nowhere to go. SO THOSE ZEROS ARE ASSERTIONS, NOT PLACEHOLDERS - the render reached those elements before the data existed. Four pages in the same wave passed the identical test (project-report, analytics, resume, assistant wrote no server figure at all while waiting), so this is a property of the page, not of the probe. THIS IS ONE INSTANCE OF A PLATFORM-WIDE PATTERN, now measured on all 22 pages: **six surfaces stamp 0 into hero tiles during load** - asset-hub, report-sender, shift-brain, skillmatrix, achievements and logbook - while fourteen do not. The shape is identical each time (a `*-hero` element written at resolvedAt === 0), which makes it one fix repeated, not six investigations. TO FINISH (batched per A15): hold the skeleton or write the dash sentinel until the read resolves. alert-hub is the reference implementation - 6 skeleton elements and ZERO bare numbers during the wait. MEASURED BY DETECTING THE WRITE, WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL. Reads are wrapped in a 5s delay and counted on resolution; a MutationObserver records every mutation whose text is purely numeric, stamped with how many reads had resolved at that moment - so 'did the page write a number before it had the data?' is a measured fact. The probe writes its own sentinel ('4242') and the reading is REFUSED unless the observer sees it; every page in this wave returned controlOK = true. THE CONTROL EXISTS BECAUSE TWO EARLIER VERSIONS LIED IN THE FLATTERING DIRECTION - one tested only the added node's own text (missing numeric leaves inside an innerHTML render), the other never attached because `document.documentElement` was null at init-script time. Both reported 0 writes on pages that visibly populated. THE ORACLE IS 'were SERVER-DERIVED numbers written', not 'were numbers written': writes to the local offline-queue badge (`wh-conn-queue`, an IndexedDB depth needing no read), decorative stage numerals and engineering-design's static catalogue `pill-count` are classified separately and excluded.

scenarios.question: IDENTITY - authN from the JWT, authZ at the server, boundaries stated as boundaries and never rendered as emptiness
scenarios.oracle: another person's object id is refused, and the refusal is legible

evidence.asserts: another person's object id is refused, and the refusal is legible
evidence.checked: PASSES. WHICH OF THE GATE'S CHECKS PROVE THIS ORACLE (named, not inherited from 'the gate is green'): OBJECT-level access: the gate's cross-tenant READ and OWN-SCOPE WRITE checks - read_logbook_xhive and read_cxp_xhive (a FOREIGN hive's v_logbook_truth and community_xp return ZERO rows) and logbook_edit_ownscope (a member cannot UPDATE another hive's logbook entry). These are per-OBJECT refusals: the caller names a specific row they do not own and is refused, which is exactly what BOLA asks. Persona under test on this row: worker (may read, not send) - and the gate's probe IS that persona, a real authenticated member of one hive reaching for another's data. WHAT WOULD HAVE FAILED IT: any one of those checks returning a row it should not, and the gate is known to fire because it was BUILT on real leaks it caught - 1,105 rows of a foreign tenant's logbook, a self-joinable membership, and a DELETE-then-reINSERT that un-banned a kicked worker. HOW IT WAS MEASURED, by REUSING the instrument the platform already owns instead of writing another: tools/validate_hive_isolation.py runs 26 invariants LIVE as a real authenticated member of one hive against a second, data-rich hive, every attempt inside a rolled-back transaction so the shared database is never polluted. Current result: 26 pass / 0 fail. IT IS ROLE-CORRECT, which is the only reason it means anything: it sets both the `authenticated` ROLE and the JWT claims. A probe carrying claims while still running as superuser bypasses RLS entirely and passes by construction - and that is not hypothetical, it cost a false finding on this very platform the same day, when an approved change order looked EDITABLE as `postgres` and is in fact refused for both a worker and a supervisor, because the guard deliberately exempts the admin path. IT IS RESEED-ROBUST: the actors and the foreign hive are resolved DYNAMICALLY from live hive_members rows rather than pinned as UUIDs, so a reseed cannot quietly turn the probe into a test of a dead hive - which would 403 for the WRONG reason and read as a pass. AND IT CARRIES NO-REGRESSION CHECKS (join_rpc_ok, founder_create_ok), so a gate that 'passed' by breaking the legitimate path would be caught rather than celebrated. WHY THIS ROW WAS STALE: it was hand-walked in an earlier session and banked with no `evidence.replay`, so nothing could re-earn it without a human repeating the whole probe. It now carries the command, which is the entire point of the A16 anti-stale discipline: 546 db-anchored rows on this platform are in exactly that position, and this is 176 of them coming out of it.

findings.title: auth_uid is bound from the JWT, but the display column worker_name is stored exactly as the body supplied it
findings.detail: MEASURED, in the same rolled-back probe that proves this row green. Writing as Hector (JWT sub 8fb252f7-...) while supplying auth_uid = Romeo's id AND worker_name = 'Romeo Beltran': the stored auth_uid was corrected to Hector's by trg_bind_submitter_logbook, and the stored worker_name remained 'Romeo Beltran'. So the authoritative identity is safe and the human-readable one is not. WHY THAT MATTERS HERE SPECIFICALLY, RATHER THAN AS A PURIST POINT: reads across this platform filter and group by worker_name, not by auth_uid - `.eq('worker_name', WORKER_NAME)` is the dominant pattern in logbook, inventory, dayplanner, skillmatrix and the resume evidence path. So a row whose worker_name disagrees with its auth_uid is attributed to the WRONG PERSON in every list that reads it, while looking perfectly consistent to any check that only inspects auth_uid. logbook is the platform's evidence base: it feeds MTBF, PM compliance and a person's resume evidence, so misattribution is not cosmetic. NOT ESCALATED TO A FAILURE because the oracle asks whether identity comes from the JWT rather than the body, and for the identity column it does. TO FINISH: either derive worker_name from auth_uid in the same trigger that already binds auth_uid (it is one lookup away and the trigger is already there), or make the reads key on auth_uid so the display name cannot drive attribution. The first is the smaller change and keeps the existing read patterns working.

scenarios.oracle: a permission boundary reads as 'not visible with this session', never as 'nothing here' - the difference between 'you may not look' and 'all clear'

evidence.asserts: no relation this page reads hides a refusal inside an empty successful response
evidence.checked: PASSES. Of this page's 2 read relation(s), 1 were probed live at the gateway (report_contacts). None of them returns an identical status and body type to an anon caller and a member, so a refusal here is observably different from absence. THE MEASURED FINDING, which is about the CONTRACT rather than a bug: on 26 of the 40 relations a REFUSAL IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM ABSENCE. An anonymous caller and an authenticated member receive the SAME status (200) and the same body TYPE (a JSON array), differing only in row count - anon 0 rows, member 2. A request with NO apikey at all also returns 200 []. So nothing in the response separates 'you are not permitted', 'you are not signed in', and 'this hive genuinely has no entries'. This is PostgREST + RLS by construction - row filtering is not request refusal - so it is not a gateway defect. It is an OBLIGATION every surface inherits: the client must decide from session state, and a page that does not will render an expired session as an empty plant. That is the read-path half of the 401-vs-403 lesson this platform already carries. The counter-example proves the point: some relations answer a refusal with 42501, a code a client can act on. HOW IT WAS MEASURED: real HTTP GETs against the LIVE local gateway (http://127.0.0.1:54321/rest/v1), 40 relations, as three personas - anonymous with the publishable key, an AUTHENTICATED member (a real minted JWT for the seeded test identity), and a request carrying NO apikey at all. GET only, so nothing is written and there is nothing to roll back. Per relation: a collection read; the same read authenticated; the same read unauthenticated; a single-object read (Accept: application/vnd.pgrst.object+json) of a row that cannot exist; a read naming a column that does not exist; and a Prefer: count=exact read. THREE NON-VACUITY CONTROLS, all passing, because a gateway that answered 200 to everything would make every verdict here free: (1) an unknown column MUST return 400 - proves the prober can observe a failure at all; (2) community_posts MUST return rows to an ANON caller, since it is the public feed - proves anon is not blanket-denied, so a 200 [] on a tenant table is RLS working rather than a dead key; (3) authenticated MUST out-read anon somewhere - without it, 'a refusal looks like absence' would be vacuously true. AND THE PROBE'S OWN FIRST RUN REPORTED TWO DEFECTS THAT WERE BOTH MINE, corrected before anything was banked. It probed ?id=eq.<uuid> on every relation, but community_xp is keyed (worker_name, hive_id) and has no id column, so the request returned 42703 'column does not exist' - my malformed query read back as the gateway's misbehaviour. And it treated projects' 42501 'insufficient privilege' as a shape violation when a refusal carrying a machine-readable code is a CORRECT envelope - on this platform it is the better behaviour. A probe that assumes a schema it never checked produces findings about itself. THESE ROWS WERE OWED ON A FALSE PREMISE, and that is worth recording because the premise was in our OWN TOOLING. Two provers documented that these oracles 'need the REST gateway, which is not reachable from this shell (kong publishes no host port)', and one copied that sentence into banked evidence. It was wrong: docker ps shows supabase_kong_workhive 0.0.0.0:54321->8000/tcp, and one curl with the publishable key answers 200. A ceiling written into a tool's docstring stops reading like a claim and starts reading like documentation, so it survived across sessions and kept ~130 rows owed. Corrected in place in both files rather than deleted.

findings.detail: MEASURED, in the same rolled-back probe that proves this row green. TO FINISH: either derive worker_name from auth_uid in the same trigger that already binds auth_uid (it is one lookup away and the trigger is already there), or make the reads key on auth_uid so the display name cannot drive attribution. evidence.asserts: no relation this page reads hides a refusal inside an empty successful response
evidence.checked: PASSES. Of this page's 2 read relation(s), 1 were probed live at the gateway (report_contacts). None of them returns an identical status and body type to an anon caller and a member, so a refusal here is observably different from absence. THE MEASURED FINDING, which is about the CONTRACT rather than a bug: on 26 of the 40 relations a REFUSAL IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM ABSENCE. An anonymous caller and an authenticated member receive the SAME status (200) and the same body TYPE (a JSON array), differing only in row count - anon 0 rows, member 2. A request with NO apikey at all also returns 200 []. So nothing in the response separates 'you are not permitted', 'you are not signed in', and 'this hive genuinely has no entries'. This is PostgREST + RLS by construction - row filtering is not request refusal - so it is not a gateway defect. It is an OBLIGATION every surface inherits: the client must decide from session state, and a page that does not will render an expired session as an empty plant. That is the read-path half of the 401-vs-403 lesson this platform already carries. The counter-example proves the point: some relations answer a refusal with 42501, a code a client can act on. HOW IT WAS MEASURED: real HTTP GETs against the LIVE local gateway (http://127.0.0.1:54321/rest/v1), 40 relations, as three personas - anonymous with the publishable key, an AUTHENTICATED member (a real minted JWT for the seeded test identity), and a request carrying NO apikey at all. GET only, so nothing is written and there is nothing to roll back. Per relation: a collection read; the same read authenticated; the same read unauthenticated; a single-object read (Accept: application/vnd.pgrst.object+json) of a row that cannot exist; a read naming a column that does not exist; and a Prefer: count=exact read. THREE NON-VACUITY CONTROLS, all passing, because a gateway that answered 200 to everything would make every verdict here free: (1) an unknown column MUST return 400 - proves the prober can observe a failure at all; (2) community_posts MUST return rows to an ANON caller, since it is the public feed - proves anon is not blanket-denied, so a 200 [] on a tenant table is RLS working rather than a dead key; (3) authenticated MUST out-read anon somewhere - without it, 'a refusal looks like absence' would be vacuously true. AND THE PROBE'S OWN FIRST RUN REPORTED TWO DEFECTS THAT WERE BOTH MINE, corrected before anything was banked. It probed ?id=eq.<uuid> on every relation, but community_xp is keyed (worker_name, hive_id) and has no id column, so the request returned 42703 'column does not exist' - my malformed query read back as the gateway's misbehaviour. And it treated projects' 42501 'insufficient privilege' as a shape violation when a refusal carrying a machine-readable code is a CORRECT envelope - on this platform it is the better behaviour. A probe that assumes a schema it never checked produces findings about itself. THESE ROWS WERE OWED ON A FALSE PREMISE, and that is worth recording because the premise was in our OWN TOOLING. Two provers documented that these oracles 'need the REST gateway, which is not reachable from this shell (kong publishes no host port)', and one copied that sentence into banked evidence. It was wrong: docker ps shows supabase_kong_workhive 0.0.0.0:54321->8000/tcp, and one curl with the publishable key answers 200. A ceiling written into a tool's docstring stops reading like a claim and starts reading like documentation, so it survived across sessions and kept ~130 rows owed. Corrected in place in both files rather than deleted.
evidence.value_checked: 1 probed relation(s), 0 indistinguishable

subject.name: bounces come back to the sender

scenarios.oracle: bounces and undeliverables are reported back

evidence.asserts: BUILT THIS WALK. Send-time rejections were already reported: a malformed address comes back from the API call and the sender reads 'failed: Invalid `to` field'. The undeliverables that matter most do not arrive that way. A full mailbox, a retired address, a domain that greylists and then gives up: the API returns 200, the supervisor sees 'sent', and the report never lands. WorkHive had no way to receive that outcome, and I had previously written this off as blocked on Resend's dashboard. The dashboard registration is genuinely Ian's to do, but everything underneath it was buildable and was missing, starting with the part that would have made the dashboard useless anyway: send-report-email obtained Resend's message id, returned it to the caller, and never stored it, so an event arriving later had NOTHING to be joined to. That correlation key is now persisted into the send's automation_log detail. On top of it, resend-webhook-receiver ingests email.bounced, email.complained and email.delivery_delayed, resolves the owning hive by matching that stored id, and records the outcome to automation_log. report-sender then reads the last 30 days of those rows and marks the affected contact in the list a supervisor actually reads: 'Last report bounced. This address did not receive it.' Two failure modes were handled deliberately: an unrecognised event type is ACKed with 200 rather than an error, because a non-2xx makes Resend retry forever something we will never handle; and a FAILED bounce read leaves the map untouched instead of rendering an empty one, since 'no bounces' and 'could not find out' are opposite claims.
evidence.checked: The signature verifier was teeth-tested against the SHIPPED source, extracted verbatim from the .ts and evaluated rather than paraphrased, across six branches: a correctly-signed Svix payload VERIFIES (the control, without which a verifier that rejects everything passes every negative case), and a tampered body, a wrong secret, a replayed timestamp an hour old, and a missing signature all fail, while a rotation header carrying two signatures whose SECOND is valid passes. Constant-time comparison is used so a byte-at-a-time forgery cannot be timed out of it. The page edit was verified by parsing every inline script block with node --check, after the extractor itself was corrected: the first attempt reported a syntax error that was my own regex matching a <script inside an HTML comment, not a fault in the page. The first placement of the bounce load was also wrong and was reverted rather than patched over: it landed inside the !HIVE_ID branch, where there is no hive to query, and it now sits on the path where the hive is known.

findings.detail: FAILS: **4 of 8** controls in the sheet present an activation target under 44x44 CSS px, and the height histogram is a single bucket - **{36: 4}**. Measured on the ACTIVATION target (inputs resolve to closest('label') where one exists). 36px IS NOW A CROSS-PAGE PATTERN, WHICH CHANGES WHERE THE FIX BELONGS: inventory's part-modal failed this same oracle with **30 of 43 controls at exactly 36px** (all `button.asset-tag`), and here 4 more land on exactly 36. Two unrelated components on two pages sharing one wrong height is a TOKEN 8px under the floor, not two local mistakes - so the fix is the shared control height, and a per-page patch would leave the rest. Worth stating plainly: this is a form filled on a phone by someone standing at a machine, and the WCAG 2.5.5 floor exists because a 36px target next to full-size ones is the one a thumb misses. THE SAME CONTRACT BUG AS dayplanner, FOUND BY ASKING WHICH OTHER PAGES SHARE THE PATTERN RATHER THAN STOPPING AT ONE. Grepping every page that carries `.modal-overlay` / `.sheet-overlay` against how often it adds `.open` put report-sender at **adds-open = 0** with overlay markup present - and the live probe confirmed it. WHAT WAS BROKEN: clicking '+ Add contact' set the sheet to display:flex and left computed **visibility: hidden** - 8 controls present, **0 visible**, full text in the DOM ('Add Contact / NAME / EMAIL / ROLE / Team / Supervisor / Engineer / Manager'), and ZERO page errors. Nothing threw; the sheet simply never appeared. THE MECHANISM IS A CASCADE COLLISION, not a missing call. components.css:165 groups `.modal, .modal-content, .modal-overlay, .sheet-overlay, [role=dialog]`, and the shared rules gate visibility on `.open`: `.sheet-overlay:not(.open) { visibility: hidden }` against `.sheet-overlay.open { visibility: visible }`. This page also defines its OWN `.sheet-overlay` (report-sender.html:196) - position, inset, background, display:flex - but never declares visibility, and `:not(.open)` (class + pseudo-class) OUT-SPECIFIES a bare class selector anyway. So a local rule that looked complete could not win a property it never mentioned. THE FIX, SYMMETRIC: `overlay.classList.add('open')` in openSheet beside the existing display assignment, and `classList.remove('open')` in closeSheet - without the second, the sheet keeps visibility:visible behind display:none and the next open transitions from the wrong state. VERIFIED BOTH WAYS, THROUGH THE PATH THE PAGE ACTUALLY USES: open -> class 'sheet-overlay open', visibility VISIBLE, 8 controls, readable form. Close -> class 'sheet-overlay', visibility hidden, display none. The close verification needed a second attempt: my first check looked for `[onclick*="closeSheet"]` and this page wires close through addEventListener, so nothing was clicked and the sheet looked stuck. Dispatching the backdrop click the listener actually watches for closed it correctly. **A close path that is 'not proven' because the probe pressed the wrong thing is not a broken close path** - and reporting it as one would have been a fabricated regression on top of a real fix. WHY THIS PAGE MATTERS MORE THAN MOST: report-sender's whole purpose is sending reports to contacts, and this sheet is how a contact is added. Unopenable, the page cannot acquire a new recipient at all - and it is the one surface in the roster whose primary action is outward and irreversible.

findings.title: FAILS: 4 of 8 effective tap targets inside #sheet-overlay are under the platform's own 44px floor - button.label-pill active 59.6x36 via own box; button.label-pill 88.6x36 via own box; button.label-pill 77.3x36 via own box; button.label-pill 79.2x36 via own box. THIS IS MEASURED ON THE SAME RULER TH
findings.detail: FAILS: 4 of 8 effective tap targets inside #sheet-overlay are under the platform's own 44px floor - button.label-pill active 59.6x36 via own box; button.label-pill 88.6x36 via own box; button.label-pill 77.3x36 via own box; button.label-pill 79.2x36 via own box. THIS IS MEASURED ON THE SAME RULER THAT PASSED 750 of 750 AT PAGE LEVEL: the rule is ported verbatim from the V1 prover, so these are controls the platform's own standard would reject, in a view V1 never opened.  HOW IT WAS MEASURED, and why these rows sat owed for so long: CJ was measured platform-wide at V1 and banked there, and V2/V3 stayed owed for ONE reason - nobody could open those views. Resolving all 15 dialog open paths (each read from SOURCE, never matched by label) removed that blocker, and the same measurements now run inside the OPENED dialog. The open-path table lives in tools/dialog_targets.mjs, shared with the modal-exit prover so the two cannot drift apart. SCOPED TO THE DIALOG, NOT THE PAGE, which is the whole point: a dialog OVERLAYS the page, so measuring document.body with a sheet open would re-measure V1 and bank it as V2 - the one-reading-for-every-layer error this bank has already paid for once. Every measurement is rooted at the dialog element. Overflow compares each visible descendant's right edge against the dialog's own content box, with a 1px tolerance (an earlier arc counted a 0.109px abutment as occlusion) and honours overflow-x auto/scroll/hidden/clip on an ancestor INSIDE the dialog, because a deliberately scrollable panel is not a defect. THE TAP-TARGET RULE IS PORTED VERBATIM FROM THE V1 PROVER, NOT REINVENTED, and that correction is why this number means anything. The first cut omitted four of V1's exclusions - sr-only, disabled, the actionable check, and the WCAG 2.5.5 inline-link-in-prose exception - and REPLACED a control's rect with its label instead of UNIONING them. Applying a stricter standard at V2 than at V1 does not find defects, it manufactures a difference between the two views and calls it one. With V1's exact rule restored the count came back IDENTICAL, which is what makes these findings real rather than an artifact: they are measured on the same ruler that banked 750/750 at page level. SCOPE: 390px only, the mobile-first width. w641/w1280 for these views are NOT claimed by this run. Two of the 15 dialogs are UNGRADED with their reason recorded rather than counted - resume's #review-sheet has no read-only path in (it needs the upload -> resume-extract pipeline, which WRITES) and hive's #handover-sheet cannot be reached at all. The walk is NON-WRITING: it opens a dialog, measures, and presses Escape.

scenarios.oracle: the component's loading state is distinguishable from its empty state

findings.title: NOT BANKED - component_loading was induced and the page FAILED it
findings.detail: The state was induced under the fenced states() sweep - REST reads delayed a bounded 1100ms, sampled mid-flight, navigation fence verified held - and this page returned ok=false rather than a null. That distinction is the whole point: null means there was no such state to show and is banked declared-na, while FALSE means the state exists and is wrong. WHAT FALSE MEANS PER ORACLE. component_loading false: the surface did not distinguish loading from EMPTY, so a reader mid-read is shown an invitation to act on data that has not arrived. component_disabled false: a control that presents as disabled still fired its handler on a real (never forced) click, which is a control that lies. component_busy false: the action went in flight with no busy state, so a second submit is invited - and on a surface where the action is a write, that is the double-submit class. Row stays owed; the fix comes first and the row is earned after.
findings.observed: component_loading ok=false under a fenced, bounded induction

evidence.asserts: the component reaches a settled, populated state - no node is left in a permanent loading or skeleton shimmer, and the states the page announces during load (skeleton, aria-busy, disabled) are the ones it actually uses

So a page reporting 0 skeletons has PROVEN it can see one. Measuring after settle is how 'this page has no loading state' gets recorded for a page that paints nine skeleton rows during load - hive did exactly that, and a candidate now counts as a skeleton only at placeholder GEOMETRY (>=24px both axes, or an explicit skeleton/shimmer class), because an 8px dot is a status light and a 648x260 block is a skeleton

findings.detail: LIVE MCP BROWSER walk, 2026-08-06, /workhive/report-sender.html. STILL OWED - and this entry CORRECTS THE CAUSE I ASSERTED IN MY PREVIOUS PASS ON THIS SAME ROW, before that misdiagnosis turned into a wrong fix. WHAT STANDS: on the real cold load, with the instrument armed correctly (MutationObserver on `document`, arming proven in-output at 15.7ms / readyState 'loading' - my earlier watchers armed at 'interactive' and were blind ~650ms), the shared wh-skeleton IS inserted into #history-list at 423.3ms and removed at 544.7ms, carrying aria-busy="true" and aria-live="polite". And the correctly-armed rAF sampler saw a visible skeleton on ZERO of 790 frames. So the oracle still fails: across a 121ms window nothing was ever painted, therefore nothing was reserved. WHAT I GOT WRONG: I reported the cause as '#history-list is collapsed or unsized at the moment the skeleton is placed into it, so the four 44px rows cannot claim height', and proposed a min-height on #history-list. I tested that claim instead of shipping it, and it is FALSE. Emptying #history-list at rest and calling the page's own whListSkeleton(el, 4) renders 408x208 - a wrapper at 408x208, four rows at 408x44 each, display flex, aria-busy and aria-live present, and the .wh-skeleton-row CSS rule confirmed matching. The container is 408 wide and takes its height from the skeleton exactly as designed. There is no CSS defect here and min-height would have been a no-op. AND THE 0x0 I MEASURED WAS AN INSTRUMENT ARTIFACT, not the page: I read getBoundingClientRect() INSIDE the MutationObserver callback, which runs as a microtask before style and layout are resolved for the newly inserted subtree, so it returned 0x0. pm-scheduler showed the same 0x0-at-insertion followed by 9 visible frames, which was the tell I should have followed rather than explained away. Geometry must be measured on the NEXT animation frame after insertion, never in the observer callback. SO THE CAUSE IS NOW HONESTLY UNKNOWN, and that is recorded rather than guessed a second time. The leading hypothesis - untested, therefore not asserted - is that #history-section (the ancestor) is not yet rendered or is hidden during the 423-545ms window and only becomes visible once history data arrives; every ancestor I checked was visible at REST (9s in: #history-list 408x512, #history-section 540 tall, no display:none, no <details>), but rest is not the window that matters. TO CLOSE: log #history-section's and #history-list's computed display plus their boxes on every frame from an early-armed rAF across the 400-560ms window, and read the actual reason out of that timeline. Only then propose a fix. The one thing now established is that the shared component is NOT at fault - inventory renders the identical helper at 960x208, visible on 6 frames, in the same sweep.

findings.title: NOT BANKED - component_disabled was induced and the page FAILED it
findings.detail: The state was induced under the fenced states() sweep - REST reads delayed a bounded 1100ms, sampled mid-flight, navigation fence verified held - and this page returned ok=false rather than a null. That distinction is the whole point: null means there was no such state to show and is banked declared-na, while FALSE means the state exists and is wrong. WHAT FALSE MEANS PER ORACLE. component_loading false: the surface did not distinguish loading from EMPTY, so a reader mid-read is shown an invitation to act on data that has not arrived. component_disabled false: a control that presents as disabled still fired its handler on a real (never forced) click, which is a control that lies. component_busy false: the action went in flight with no busy state, so a second submit is invited - and on a surface where the action is a write, that is the double-submit class. Row stays owed; the fix comes first and the row is earned after.

findings.title: MEASURED INSIDE THIS VIEW, with tools/prove_view_contrast.mjs - 34 of 37 drivable registry views carried text to measure, ZERO failing.
findings.detail: MEASURED INSIDE THIS VIEW, with tools/prove_view_contrast.mjs - 34 of 37 drivable registry views carried text to measure, ZERO failing. ★WHY A VIEW-SCOPED PROVER HAD TO BE BUILT FOR THIS: a page-level sweep of all 22 pages (tools/prove_page_contrast.mjs) found the platform clean and settled NOTHING here, because every owed contrast row in these banks is authored against V2 or V3 - the dialogs - while their V1 siblings were already green. Banking a page-default reading onto a V2 row is the one-measurement-swept-two-views error that has already put 14 rows in this bank carrying another view's verdict. The view is opened through tools/dialog_targets.mjs, the same shared registry ten other provers use, so the view graded here is the view they grade. WCAG 2.x is measured with the composited probe: the background is blended UP the ancestor chain, because a translucent tint over a dark card is not the colour the stylesheet names, and text over a gradient is recorded as UNMEASURABLE rather than being compared against a canvas it never sits on - the shape that once reported ratio exactly 1.00 for perfectly legible text. NOT BANKED: this view yielded ZERO measurable samples (1 unmeasurable), so there is no denominator and a pass would be vacuous. The cause is structural rather than a probe fault, and it was verified by tracing the paint chain: the dialog's inner card is a TRANSLUCENT GRADIENT - linear-gradient(145deg, rgba(42,61,88,0.6) ...) - over a rgba(0,0,0,0.75) scrim over the page. WCAG 2.x is a ratio between TWO colours, and there is no single background colour here to be the second one. THE APCA SIBLING OF THIS ROW IS NOT AFFECTED and was measured normally, because that lens averages the gradient's stops instead of demanding one flat colour - which is why the platform treats APCA as the primary contrast oracle on this dark shell. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: sample the RENDERED PIXELS around each glyph from a screenshot of this view, which is the only way to obtain the real second colour behind text that sits on a gradient. That is a buildable instrument, not a ceiling - it is simply not built yet, and this row stays owed until it is.

findings.title: NOT BANKED, BECAUSE THE PASS IS VACUOUS ON THIS VIEW - and the prover's own numbers are what show it.
findings.detail: NOT BANKED, BECAUSE THE PASS IS VACUOUS ON THIS VIEW - and the prover's own numbers are what show it. tools/prove_dialog_a11y.mjs graded 36 of 43 registry targets with ZERO failing, and its summary line reads 'every focusable control shows a causally-verified focus indicator'. On this view that sentence is true the way any statement about an empty set is true: the report records focus.candidates = 0 and focus.checked = 0. No focusable control was examined, so nothing about focus indication was established. Banking it green would put a row in the bank whose evidence is an empty denominator - the exact false green this bank exists to prevent. THIS IS A PROPERTY OF THE VIEW, NOT A DEFECT. Six of the thirty-six graded views hold no focusable controls at all - engineering-design's guide tab, shift-brain's verdict summary and its details disclosure, report-sender's contacts list, public-feed's feed list, achievements' recent list. They are READ surfaces: text, cards and figures. A view with nothing to focus cannot fail a focus oracle, and it cannot pass one either. WORTH SEPARATING FROM THE SIBLING ORACLES, because they are NOT vacuous here: this same run measured accessible names and reduced-motion on the same views and those are real readings - a name applies to any control, focusable or not, and 'nothing animates under prefers-reduced-motion' is a statement about the whole subtree. So the a11y run is only empty for FOCUS on these six. WHAT WOULD SETTLE THIS ROW: either the view genuinely gains an interactive control (then re-run and grade it), or the row is dispositioned declared-na with this reason under R10 - which needs a replacement oracle named, and the honest replacement is that the view is READABLE and its figures are labelled (CL contrast + CM what_is_this_number), not that its focus ring works. AND AN INSTRUMENT NOTE, since the prover is otherwise strong: its per-view PASS does not distinguish 'checked N controls, all good' from 'checked none'. The distinction is recoverable only from focus.candidates in the report, so a consumer that reads the exit code alone would bank all six of these as proven. The count belongs in the printed line.

findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_what_happens_next.mjs across the roster: 22 pass, 2 PARTIAL (recorded and left OWED rather than rounded up), 0 fail - and NO WRITE REACHED THE DATABASE. ★THE ORACLE IS ABOUT WHAT A PERSON KNOWS BEFORE THEY COMMIT, not after. A control that says 'Save' and then produces something the person did not expect has failed them at the moment the choice was made, which is the only moment they could have chosen differently. ★AND THE PARTIALS ARE THE HONEST PART: two surfaces tell part of the story, and they are left OWED with that recorded. Rounding a partial up to a pass is how a bank stops meaning anything - the whole point of a %% here is that it is computed from verdicts nobody softened. ★SAFETY: this prover ACTS on a live product (it presses controls), so every mutating request is counted and held. An earlier sweep on this platform went hunting for a refusal and ACTIVATED A SUCCESS because its filter excluded delete/pay but not save/generate. FOR THIS PAGE: at least one control tells only PART of what happens next - recorded and left owed rather than rounded up: [{"page": "report-sender", "confirmationRank": 0, "message": "Generating... | All reports failed, check connection and try again", "fired": 1, "edge": 1, "hasNext": true, "hasWhen": false, "status": " ★RE-WALKED AFTER THIS SESSION'S TWELVE PRODUCT FIXES so the evidence carries digests of the code as it now stands - R4b expired the prior rows because the fixes changed the functions they rested on.
