evidence.asserts: after pressing Send Reports the surface says what happened, to whom, and what happens next with when - and a failure says why rather than only that it failed
evidence.checked: WALKED LIVE with EVERY send-report-email invoke INTERCEPTED and fulfilled locally - no email left this machine, which is non-negotiable on the one action this platform cannot undo. THE FULL LEGIBLE SEQUENCE, sampled at 1s: +1016ms the main card is data-state='processing' with Send disabled and the status row still hidden (report generation); +2035ms the invoke fires (1 send) and the status row becomes VISIBLE reading 'Sending email...'; +3050ms it reads 'Sent to probe.held@example.invalid' with class 'email-status sent' and a live countdown 'Resetting in 12s'. So the terminal state names WHO received it, that it completed, and what happens next WITH its timing - the countdown is the 'when' this oracle asks for, and it ticks. Multi-recipient collapses to '<N> recipients' and a partial failure appends ' (N failed)'. THE REFUSAL IS BY PREVENTION, worth recording because it is not a message: Send is disabled until both a report and a recipient exist, so pressing it with nothing selected produced 0 sends and no error text - the control simply cannot be fired. FAILURE PATH MEASURED SEPARATELY (forced 500): status reads 'Email failed: <reason>' with class 'email-status error' and NO countdown, so a receipt carrying a failure never auto-wipes - which is the deliberate Y2 behaviour its own comment claims (full success auto-resets on 12s; failures wait for a manual reset). A DEFECT WAS FOUND AND FIXED HERE: both send paths did throw new Error((data && data.error) || error.message) under a comment asserting invoke() 'surfaces a non-2xx as error while still parsing the body into data'. Measured, it does not - on a 500 whose body was {"error":"mail relay refused the message"}, data carried no error and the supervisor was shown the transport's sentence, 'Email failed: Edge Function returned a non-2xx status code'. The real cause was in the response body and discarded. Added a local _fnErrorReason(data, error, fallback) that falls back to error.context (the raw Response in supabase-js v2, cloned because a body can only be consumed once); re-measured, the same forced failure now reads 'Email failed: mail relay refused the message'. Kept LOCAL to report-sender.html rather than utils.js on purpose: utils.js is a shared dependency of every page bank, and a one-page helper there would expire roughly 300 unrelated rows under R4 for no gain.

findings.title: NOT BANKED - why_refused needs a refusal INDUCED and the probe induced none (refusedCalls 0, vacuous). Probe built; its submit-finder is the remaining work
findings.detail: A REFUSAL DOES NOT EXIST ON A SETTLED PAGE, so this oracle cannot be observed - it has to be INDUCED. comprehension().refusals returns an EMPTY ARRAY on all 20 pages for exactly that reason: nothing has been refused yet. Banking '0 of 0 refusals lack a reason' would be vacuously true, and banking it as a pass is how coverage improves by deleting obligations. So a probe was built for it - window.__wh7.whyRefused() - which answers every mutating verb locally with a 403 in the PostgREST permission shape (code 42501, 'permission denied for table'), drives a submit, and reads what the page TELLS the person. No write is forwarded, so nothing reaches the shared test database. THE ORACLE IT ENCODES, which is worth keeping even though the row is still owed: 403 IS NOT 401. Under RLS a 403 means the session is ALIVE and this action is not permitted, so 'sign in again' is the wrong answer and sends someone to fix the one thing that is not broken. This platform already learned that in the other direction - a 42501 once told a signed-in buyer their session had expired. A good refusal names the PERMISSION or the ROLE. The probe therefore reports saysRefused, namesReason and blamesSession separately, and requires (saysRefused OR namesReason) AND NOT blamesSession. WHY THE ROW IS STILL OWED, stated exactly: refusedCalls came back 0 on all four pages plus logbook and pm-scheduler, so NOTHING was ever refused and the verdict is stamped vacuous:true with ok forced to null rather than false. The probe is honest about having no subject; it is not reporting a pass. TWO CONCRETE DEFECTS IN THE PROBE, both found by measuring rather than reasoning, and both fixed or named: (1) it reused m() and navigatesAway(), which are LOCAL to overflow()/tapTargets() in that file, so it threw ReferenceError - and the crash hit report-sender, the ONE page of six that had any submit candidate at all. A staged try/catch reporting CRASH_AT:probe instead of a bare REJ is what separated a broken probe from a blocked page; without it, six pages looked uniformly refused when the probe had simply crashed. Both scope bugs are fixed. (2) THE TARGET-FINDER IS TOO LOOSE and that is the remaining work: its selector list includes [id*="send"], which matched 'report-sender-source-chip' - the page's own NAME contains 'send'. A source chip submits nothing, which is precisely why refusedCalls stayed 0 on the one page that looked promising. TO FINISH THIS ROW: replace substring id matching with real submit semantics - button[type=submit] inside a form, or a control whose onclick names a save/send/submit FUNCTION (the same read-the-markup approach that fixed the V2 openers after class-name guesses all missed) - and drive it from inside an OPEN form view, since these list surfaces have no submit control at all. Opening the form first was tried here (openUseModal / openModal / openDetail) and still yielded 0 refused calls, so the modal's own save control needs naming per page rather than discovering generically. Row stays owed.
findings.observed: whyRefused(): refusedCalls 0, submitUsed null (report-sender matched 'report-sender-source-chip' via a loose [id*=send] selector), ok null, vacuous true. Also fixed two ReferenceErrors from reusing function-local helpers (m, navigatesAway) at module scope.

findings.detail: FAILS: with 11 of this page's reads answered 403/42501, it says NOTHING AT ALL - the body text is 1876 characters before the refusal and 1407 after, and no new sentence explains anything.  WHAT THIS ORACLE IS REALLY FOR, and the good news first: it checks that a refusal names PERMISSION rather than IDENTITY, because this platform has already shipped that exact inversion - a 42501 rendered as 'your session has expired', which sends a signed-IN person to re-authenticate for a problem authentication cannot fix, and 401/403 collapsed into one message so neither audience got a true statement. ZERO of the 16 graded pages made that mistake on this run. utils.js:1607 whIsAuthFailure() is why: it returns FALSE for status 403 with the comment 'authenticated, and refused. Not a session problem', and documents 42501 as insufficient_privilege. That discrimination is holding. HOW THE REFUSAL WAS INDUCED, and why it is the real branch: every Supabase REST read is answered with the body PostgREST actually sends for a row-level-security refusal - HTTP 403 with {"code":"42501","message":"permission denied for table"} - so the page's own error handling takes the same path it would in production. The patch is on window.fetch, NOT page.route, because a warm service worker serves from cache and bypasses route interception; it is installed with addInitScript in a context closed after each page so it cannot leak. NON-WRITING: it makes a READ return 403. THE INJECTION PROVES ITSELF: every intercepted call increments a counter, and a page where the counter is zero is UNGRADED rather than judged. That guard exists because the first version of this prover silently did nothing - a regex written inside a template literal collapsed to one that terminates at its second character, so the init script was a SyntaxError, every read succeeded normally, and the prover reported 'the reads were all refused and the page said nothing' while nothing had been refused at all. Hit counts on this run ranged from 8 to 42 per page. AND THE SIGNAL MUST APPEAR: the same page is read WITHOUT the injection first, and if its ordinary copy already matches the refusal vocabulary the page is UNGRADED - which is exactly what happened to skillmatrix, whose normal text contains a matching phrase. Without that control a page whose everyday copy happens to say 'cannot' would pass for free. THE SYNTHESIS - THIS IS ONE MISSING SURFACE, NOT 15 PAGE BUGS. Of 16 graded pages: 13 said NOTHING AT ALL when every read was refused, 2 showed only a GENERIC error ('Analysis failed, check console'; 'Achievements failed to load.'), and 1 passed. The platform already has the pieces - a central WRITE-failure message and the correct 401-vs-403 discriminator in utils.js - but there is no equivalent on the READ path, so a refused read renders as dashes or blanks with no explanation. On logbook the numbers '516 entries 30 machines 6 open' became '- entries - machines - open' with the body text identical to the character (1107 before and after) and not one word about why. A person cannot tell 'there is no data' from 'the load failed' from 'you are not allowed', and those three call for three different actions. THE FIX IS ONE ADOPTION, not 15 edits: give the read path the same treatment the write path already has. This independently reproduces a finding already recorded as 'the message already exists; the gap is ADOPTION on the read path'. SCOPE: V1, the page as it loads, and READ refusal only - a refused WRITE is a different path with its own central message, and is not claimed here. 5 of the 22 pages are excluded from the sweep because they are public or have no authenticated read to refuse. The walk is NON-WRITING.

evidence.asserts: after adding a contact, the surface names what changes and when
evidence.checked: LIVE WALK. Opened the contacts sheet with #add-contact-btn, filled #contact-name and #contact-email, pressed #save-contact-btn with the write delayed then answered synthetically. Confirmation: 'WH Probe Contact added → in your recipient list now, and saved for future reports.' It names the effect (the contact joins the recipient list), WHEN ('now'), and that it persists for later sends. I WROTE THAT SENTENCE THIS WALK. The shipped copy was '<name> added' - added to WHAT, usable WHEN? The new sentence claims only what the handler verifiably does on the lines below it: push onto _contacts, renderContacts(), updateSendBtn(), and persist to localStorage so it survives navigation. TWO INSTRUMENT FAULTS CAME FIRST, both mine. (1) My synthetic responder read init.headers.Accept, but init.headers is a Headers INSTANCE, so the check silently failed and a .single() insert was answered with an ARRAY - data.name was then undefined and renderContacts() threw 'name is not iterable' BEFORE showToast could run, which the prover reported as the surface saying nothing at all. A synthetic success that is not shaped like the real service tests the FAILURE path and calls it the success path. Fixed by honouring Accept: application/vnd.pgrst.object+json the way PostgREST does. (2) My NEXT vocabulary had 'on your <schedule>' but not 'in your <list>' - the same construction naming where an effect lands - so a correct sentence scored as naming no following step. Widened to the platform's own wording rather than bending the product's sentence to fit the regex.

value_checked.confirmation: WH Probe Contact added → in your recipient list now, and saved for future reports.

findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs - 66 persona-journeys attempted across the roster. ★AND FIFTY OF THEM ARE NOT FINDINGS: they read 'journey could not be constructed: browser.newContext: Target page, context or browser has been closed', which is the harness dying mid-run, not a page failing a person. The run was killed twice - once by my own 570-second timeout and once when the backgrounded process lost its browser - and BOTH times it emitted those as FAILs. A probe whose browser is shot out from under it reports every remaining page as broken. ★SO THEY ARE NOT BANKED. Fifty false reds would have read as the worst finding of the session, and the only thing separating them from a real one is that I read the verdict string instead of the count. This is the same discipline as refusing a zero from a request counter a service worker was bypassing: an instrument that has stopped working reports the world as broken. ★WHAT IS BANKED IS THE SIXTEEN THAT ACTUALLY WALKED, plus the sub-journeys that completed: two_sided 15 walked / 0 failing, handoff 14 walked / 0 failing, abandon 7 walked / 1 failing. Those are real readings of a live product. FOR THIS PAGE: every journey attempt died with the harness, so nothing was measured here. Recorded as UNWALKED, never as failing - the difference between 'this page failed a person' and 'my browser closed' is the whole value of this row. ★RE-WALKED AFTER THIS SESSION'S TWELVE PRODUCT FIXES so the evidence carries digests of the code as it now stands. Re-WALKED, never re-baselined.

The run was killed twice - once by my own 570-second timeout and once when the backgrounded process lost its browser - and BOTH times it emitted those as FAILs. A probe whose browser is shot out from under it reports every remaining page as broken. ★SO THEY ARE NOT BANKED. Fifty false reds would have read as the worst finding of the session, and the only thing separating them from a real one is that I read the verdict string instead of the count. Those are real readings of a live product. FOR THIS PAGE: every journey attempt died with the harness, so nothing was measured here. findings.title: MEASURED with tools/prove_session_died.mjs: 14 pages measured, NONE presents a dead session as signed-in data.
findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_session_died.mjs: 14 pages measured, NONE presents a dead session as signed-in data. EIGHT are UNGRADED and listed, NOT counted. ★THE UNGRADED ARE THE HONEST PART. A page that has not finished rendering is not a page that failed - one of them showed 0 busy elements and 371 chars six seconds in, and scoring that as a defect would manufacture a finding out of a slow host. This prover previously printed 'PASS - no page presents a dead session as signed-in data' over ZERO measurements, because its regexes were declared in Node scope and referenced inside page.evaluate, so every page threw ReferenceError and came back ungraded while `bad.length === 0` did the work. An empty graded set now exits non-zero and says so. ★WHAT IT CATCHES IS THE WORST QUIET FAILURE ON A LOGGED-IN PRODUCT: a session that has expired while the page keeps rendering the numbers it fetched before, so a supervisor reads a confident dashboard that belongs to nobody. banked ONLY for the 15 of 22 pages where killing the session visibly changed the page. The prover measures the SAME page signed-in first as its non-vacuity control, and the 7 pages it could not distinguish are NOT banked here: public-feed and project-report render no non-zero values even WITH a session, and engineering-design is identical either way because its surviving figures are client-computed calculator values, not hive data.
